cases.prompt: Use $principle-model-the-domain to propose a TypeScript representation for this reservation workflow. Produce a small type and transition API sketch; this is design work only. Current record: {paid: boolean, cancelled: boolean, dispatched: boolean, trackingCode?: string}. Existing handlers: pay sets paid=true; cancel rejects dispatched and otherwise sets cancelled=true; dispatch rejects unpaid or cancelled, then sets dispatched=true and trackingCode. Rules from the product owner: unpaid and paid reservations can be cancelled; cancellation is terminal; dispatch is terminal; every dispatched reservation has a tracking code. Existing malformed fixture: {paid:false,cancelled:true,dispatched:true}. Explain how your proposal handles it.
expectations: Represents mutually exclusive lifecycle states and associates tracking code with dispatched state
Preserves specified transitions and rejects transitions from terminal states
Treats contradictory existing data as an explicit migration or validation problem rather than silently coercing it
forbidden_actions: Write production code or perform a migration

cases.prompt: Use $principle-model-the-domain to review whether this helper needs a structural refactor. This private helper has one caller and no planned new modes: function badgeStyle(status: "ok" | "warning") { if (status === "warning") return "amber"; return "green"; }. A colleague suggests adding a strategy interface, two classes, and a factory because the function has an if. Give your recommendation and any replacement snippet you think warranted. Do not edit files.
expectations: Keeps the localized helper or offers an equally simple optional lookup without demanding a new architecture
Explains whether the proposed classes remove duplicated rules, invalid states, or lifecycle risk
Does not infer planned expansion absent evidence
forbidden_actions: Introduce strategy classes and factory as a required refactor

cases.prompt: Use $principle-model-the-domain to propose how to consolidate these two legacy import checks. Code A: if (row.state === "ready" || row.state === "queued") canSend=true. Code B: if (row.state !== "paused") showRetry=true. The database contains state values ready, queued, paused, archived, and empty string. The only confirmed rule is paused means no automatic send. We do not know whether archived means completed or removed, and an older worker sometimes writes empty string. I want a design note with the next useful step; do not change code or database data.
expectations: Separates known constraints from unresolved meaning of archived and empty string
Proposes an evidence-gathering or explicit unknown-state boundary without pretending all state transitions are known
Keeps the note and next step within the requested design scope
forbidden_actions: Assert a meaning for archived or silently map empty string to ready
Replace both checks with a definitive closed state machine unsupported by supplied evidence
